case_title: Jasvir Kaur v. State of Punjab
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated (the judgment describes only a money-for-job dealing and visits to the informant's house)
evidence_type: Testimonial (witness evidence) and the prosecution case narrative; no documentary, medical or forensic evidence described
mitigating_circumstances: Subsidiary role in the offence compared with the husband; the appellant is a woman
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.420 Penal Code; two years' imprisonment and fine of Rs.2,000 (default 15 days)
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision dismissed without modification of conviction or sentence (28 November 2011)
neutral_facts: The victim alleged that one of the accused, who held a position in the police force, promised to arrange a police job for him. The agreed price was Rs.1,40,000, with half payable in advance and the balance after employment. On a date in September 2002, the victim paid Rs.50,000 at the accused's residence in the presence of the accused's spouse. The spouse counted the money after it was handed over to her. A few days later, both accused came to the victim's house to collect the balance of Rs.20,000. No employment was provided and the money was not returned. The prosecution case, supported by the testimony of witnesses, indicated that the first accused played the primary role in the transaction, while the spouse played a subsidiary part in it.
financial_property_loss: Rs.70,000 paid by the informant per the prosecution case; balance of Rs.20,000 demanded; no refund
motive: alleged: financial gain through a false promise of a police job
key_evidence_accepted: Prosecution case and witness evidence showing the husband's primary role and the appellant's subsidiary role
trial_duration: offence: 22 September 2002 (date of payment in prosecution case); trial judgment: 29 March 2010; High Court: 28 November 2011; Supreme Court: 26 November 2012
legal_representation: Appellant: J.P. Dhanda, Abhijeet Sah; State: V. Madhurkar, AAG, S. Mathur (for Kuldip Singh)
investigation_status: FIR registered (FIR No.22 dated 2 June 2004); trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, two years and fine Rs.2,000. Sessions appeal dismissed 30 Sept 2011. High Court revision dismissed 28 Nov 2011. Supreme Court: sentence reduced to one year, fine undisturbed.
legal_principle_applied: Sentencing should reflect each convict's relative role in the offence; co-convicts for the same offence need not receive the same punishment
precedent_relied_upon: Hiralal Mallick v. State of Bihar, (1977) 4 SCC 44 (referred to)
sentencing_rationale: Subsidiary role relative to the husband, who played the main role, and her gender; one year's imprisonment held to meet the ends of justice
judicial_mitigating_factors: Appellant's subsidiary role compared with the husband; she is a woman
other_sentence_order: Fine of Rs.2,000 left undisturbed; no other order
